hpi: {{patient_name}} is an elderly patient with cardiovascular risk factors who presents with acute LLQ abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea following a meal (postprandial pain). Ischemic colitis is the most common form of GI ischemia — caused by non-occlusive hypoperfusion of the watershed areas (splenic flexure = Griffith's point, rectosigmoid = Sudeck's point). Differentiate from acute mesenteric ischemia (small bowel — embolic, more severe, pain out of proportion). CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast shows segmental colonic wall thickening, thumbprinting (submucosal edema/hemorrhage). Colonoscopy confirms with segmental erythema, ulceration. Most cases are self-limited and resolve with supportive care: bowel rest (NPO), IV fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics (cover gram-neg + anaerobes if severe). Surgery only if transmural infarction, perforation, peritonitis, or stricture.
